headline: Google Home integrates with ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI agents
summary: Google Home now supports any AI agent using Model Context Protocol, allowing them to control devices and use speakers as their voice. Access requires a $20/month subscription.
details: Google announced that Google Home will now support any AI agent that uses the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This opens the door for popular AI models like ChatGPT, Claude, and others to control smart home devices, analyze summaries, and build custom dashboards.

AI agents can now use a Google Home speaker as their "voice" for interactions. This integration extends to all devices within the Google Home ecosystem, including Nest devices, Matter devices, and any product labeled "Works with Google Home."

Taylor Lehman, product manager at Google Home & Nest, stated this is "just the next step in unlocking agentic smart homes." The feature is currently rolling out in the US and requires a $20 per month Google Home Premium Advanced subscription.

To get started, users with the subscription need to create a Google Cloud project and configure it to use MCP. The agent will then prompt the user to sign in and grant necessary permissions. Setup guides are available in the Google Home Developer Center.

While powerful, connecting AI agents to smart home controls raises privacy and security concerns. Google Home MCP prohibits sensitive actions like unlocking doors, but unexpected or undesired behavior may still occur depending on the specific agent.

headline: Judge questions Musk's companies dropping antitrust suit against Apple
summary: A federal judge is seeking details on any potential agreement that led to Musk's companies dropping their antitrust claims against Apple, demanding transparency in the legal proceedings.
details: Federal judge Mark Pittman has requested further information regarding the circumstances surrounding Elon Musk's companies dropping their antitrust lawsuit against Apple.
The judge is scrutinizing the situation to understand if there was any underlying agreement or settlement that prompted the dismissal of the legal action.
This development comes amid ongoing legal battles and scrutiny of major tech companies' practices and potential anti-competitive behaviors.
The specifics of any such agreement are now under judicial review, aiming to ensure fairness and transparency in the legal process.
